clue.text: Suitable jumper medium? Find out here

definitions.text: Suitable jumper medium? Find out here

parts.note: suitable means fitting, apt
a jumper here is a kangaroo, a roo, not a sweater
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether a sweater in size medium will suit them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like the sweater, but in the wordplay it is a leaping roo; the whole clue then describes the shop booth where you try clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop's changing cubicle is exactly where a shopper discovers whether a medium sweater suits.

clue.text: Given up working in smithy

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a smithy is a blacksmith's forge
on means working, switched on

explanation.surface: A blacksmith has stopped working in the smithy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given up working' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'Given up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relinquished or done without has been sacrificed, i.e. given up.

clue.text: Secure half of trunks on ship

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word is its first three letters

parts.note: SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Fastening half the luggage trunks aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind tightly, as a chicken's legs for roasting, is to secure it.

clue.text: Raids in Greek island reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: News of raids happening on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Incursions into enemy territory are attacks, hence raids.

clue.text: Usage so versatile, like some elements

indicators.note: versatile means adaptable, able to take a new form

explanation.surface: Remarks on flexible usage, as of chemical elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Elements such as oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen exist as gas at room temperature.

clue.text: Cook's covering duck with very English honey?

parts.note: a duck is a nil score in cricket, the shape of O
honey and love are both terms of endearment

explanation.surface: A chef covering a duck in very English honey.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'duck' is a score of nothing, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded mitt protecting a chef's hand when lifting hot dishes.

clue.text: Note cat eating large amount

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A note about a cat that eats a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large amount' reads as one phrase, but 'large' gives L for 'eating' to put inside LION; the definition is just 'amount'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand thousand is a numerical quantity, one specific amount.

clue.text: Follower making arrangement to usurp monarch

indicators.note: making an arrangement of a word puts its letters in a new order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: A courtier plots to usurp the king and seize the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making arrangement' rearranges USURP into PURSU, then ER (Elizabeth Regina, the Queen) is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone chasing another is a follower on their trail.

clue.text: Harry Potter's agile seeing off a supernatural being

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so the letters are thrown about
seeing off means getting rid of, so these letters are taken out of the mix

explanation.surface: Harry Potter is nimble enough to fend off a supernatural creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' is not the wizard's name but the anagram signal; mix POTTERSAGILE and, by 'seeing off', remove A.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy ghost said to throw objects about is a supernatural being.

clue.text: That woman returned ring for varnish …

parts.note: that woman is she

indicators.note: returned means the word for ring is written backwards

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: She sent back the ring she'd been given in exchange for some nail varnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' writes CALL backwards. The ellipsis only links the surface into the next clue, which also uses 'ring for'.
explanation.definitionFit: A resin dissolved in alcohol, used as a glossy wood finish, is a varnish.

clue.text: Supporter of revolutionary device like Kindle bringing in fifty

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

indicators.note: bringing in means taking something inside

parts.note: the Kindle is an e-reader
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fan of a revolutionary gadget like the Kindle that sells fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leads crowd cheers for a team is a supporter.

clue.text: … ring for Charlie in 'Hair and Beauty'

indicators.note: one thing for another means it is swapped in where the other stood

parts.note: locks are hair
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A salon called 'Hair and Beauty' where someone wants a ring changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring for Charlie' means O replaces the C in LOCKS. The salon name hides that 'Hair' is the starting word and 'Beauty' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Good looks means physical attractiveness, i.e. beauty.

clue.text: Next to assistant, hiding desires

indicators.note: hiding something means holding it inside, out of sight

parts.note: an aide is an assistant
longs means desires, yearns

explanation.surface: Sitting beside an assistant who conceals what they really want.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside or adjacent to something; a positional synonym.

clue.text: European fuses creating issues

parts.note: fuses means joins together, merges

explanation.surface: European electrical fuses causing problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuses' and 'issues' read as nouns in the surface, but both are verbs: merges and comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue forth is to come out or appear, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Becoming more appealing to go in pub after good argument

indicators.note: after places the pub piece later than the good argument

parts.note: a row is an argument

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub
taken as written

explanation.surface: Going to the pub after a good argument makes someone more likeable.
explanation.definitionFit: When something grows on you, it gradually wins you over: an idiom for increasing appeal.

clue.text: With interruption of power, rather faulty speaker

indicators.note: an interruption breaks into something, so one letter is placed within another word

parts.note: rather, as in I'd rather, means sooner

explanation.surface: A loudspeaker that is somewhat faulty after a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: William Spooner, Oxford don, was famed for swapping initial sounds of words, so he is a 'faulty speaker', not a broken loudspeaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reverend Spooner gave his name to tangled slips of the tongue, making him an error-prone talker.

clue.text: Fuel company noticeably depleted French region

parts.note: gas is a fuel

indicators.note: depleted means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A French region whose energy company has visibly run short of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depleted' empties 'noticeably' to its outer letters N and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic province in southwest France, home of d'Artagnan.

clue.text: Bread is prepared for gannet, perhaps

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Bread laid out for a greedy gannet.
explanation.walkthrough: A gannet is also British slang for a glutton, which suits the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A gannet is a large diving seabird; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Plant in yard he'd water here regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A plant in the garden that a man waters here regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of HEDWATERHERE: EWTREE.
explanation.definitionFit: The yew is an evergreen conifer, so a tree is a plant.

clue.text: Some loathe a treatment room in hospital

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some patients hate a particular treatment given on the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating theatre is the surgical room in a hospital.

clue.text: Blurry photos bearing unknown retailer

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the letter is held within
blurry means out of focus, jumbled

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Fuzzy pictures carrying an unidentified seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blurry' rearranges PHOTOS to TOSHOP, and 'bearing' puts Y inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling playthings is a retailer.

clue.text: One taken up the aisle raised cry, with nothing right

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means written upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: yell is a cry
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A bride walked up the aisle raises a cry when there is no Mr Right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the aisle' suggests a wedding, but it is a supermarket aisle and a shopping cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers push a wheeled basket along each supermarket aisle.

clue.text: Where racing drivers compete enthusiastically?

definitions.meaning: racing drivers compete on a large road, a big course
doing something wholeheartedly, to a great extent

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase places drivers on a large road; idiomatically it means greatly or with gusto.

clue.text: Torrent reduced surface by delta

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a floor is a surface
Delta is D in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A river torrent near its delta has lowered the land surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts FLOOR to FLOO; 'delta' looks geographical but is just D.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge or overwhelming rush of water is a torrent.

clue.text: Comparatively thin piece of fish gutted earlier

parts.note: a fin is a part of a fish

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A thin piece of fish that was gutted earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Finer, a comparative, describes something more slender or thinner.

clue.text: Keeping close to bear, Pooh's friend set off

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

parts.note: Tigger is the bouncy tiger friend of Winnie-the-Pooh

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh's friend stays near the bear and then heads off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to bear' looks like 'near Pooh' but gives R, the last letter of 'bear'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off an alarm or an explosion is to activate it; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Give learner tips from elder animal trainer

parts.note: to hand something is to give it
L is the learner-driver abbreviation

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends

explanation.surface: An older relative passing on advice to a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' looks like advice, but it means the ends of 'elder', E and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who controls and works with a dog or other creature, e.g. a police dog's minder.

clue.text: Daughter with hidden pressure before creative social event

indicators.note: before places one piece ahead of the next

parts.note: inner means inward, hidden from view
P is the physics symbol for pressure
arty means artistic, creative

explanation.surface: A daughter under unseen pressure before an artistic event.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening meal for invited guests is a social gathering.
